newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong island protest leader feared dead-TV.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong island protest leader feared dead-TV.

text.p: Hong Kong protest leader David Chan was feared dead and another activist was flown away for medical treatment by a Japanese helicopter after they dived into the China Sea on Thursday, Hong Kong radio and Cable TV said.
"When he (David Chan) was pulled out of the water he had no heartbeat or pulse," Hong Kong Cable TV reported from the scene.
The two were among five Hong Kong activists who dived into the East China Sea as part of a protest against Japanese control of the islands, which are also claimed by China.

A Hong Kong radio correspondent on board the ship Kien Hwa 2 said in a separate broadcast that two of the activists had required first aid and that group leader Chan was unconcious. They dived from the ship when it was three miles (five km) from the islands, the government-funded radio said.

"They want to demonstrate to the Japanese that Chinese have the right to do whatever they want to do, including swimming in Chinese waters," its correspondent on board said. The five activists were wearing lifejackets, it said.
The rusty tanker was surrounded by 20 Japanese vessels, five planes and one helicopter, he said.
